bio.topic: Review: cells, movement into and out of cells, biological molecules and enzymes

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.hint: Think about what gives a plant cell its fixed shape.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is the correct formula for magnification?
questions.hint: Remember I = A × M and rearrange it.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A drawing of a cell is 30 mm long. The magnification is ×1500. Calculate the actual length of the cell in micrometres (µm).
questions.hint: Convert mm to µm first (1 mm = 1000 µm), then divide by the magnification.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: An image of a cell is 25 mm wide. The actual width of the cell is 50 µm. Calculate the magnification of the image.
questions.hint: Make sure both measurements are in the same unit before dividing.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement best defines diffusion?
options: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, as a result of their random movement
The movement of particles against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration
The movement of water only, through a partially permeable membrane
The movement of particles from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration
questions.answer: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, as a result of their random movement
questions.hint: Diffusion is passive and goes down the concentration gradient.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the process by which water molecules move across a partially permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
questions.hint: It is a special case of diffusion involving water.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: How is active transport different from diffusion?
options: It moves substances against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration
It only happens in dead cells
questions.answer: It moves substances against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration
questions.hint: Think about direction and energy.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. What happens to the cell?
options: It loses water by osmosis and becomes plasmolysed
It gains water by osmosis and bursts
It gains water and becomes turgid
Nothing happens because of the cell wall
questions.answer: It loses water by osmosis and becomes plasmolysed
questions.hint: Compare the water concentration inside and outside the cell.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A potato cylinder had a mass of 2.50 g. After 30 minutes in a salt solution its mass was 2.20 g. Calculate the percentage change in mass. Give a negative sign for a loss.
questions.hint: Percentage change = (change in mass ÷ starting mass) × 100.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which reagent is used to test for reducing sugars?
questions.hint: This test requires heating in a water bath.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What colour does iodine solution turn when starch is present?
questions.hint: Iodine solution starts orange-brown.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What colour indicates a positive result for protein in the biuret test?
questions.hint: The biuret reagent starts blue.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which elements are present in all carbohydrates?
questions.hint: Proteins contain an extra element that carbohydrates do not.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the name of the molecule that binds to the active site of an enzyme.
questions.hint: It is the molecule that the enzyme acts on.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why the activity of an enzyme decreases above its optimum temperature.
options: The shape of the active site changes so the substrate no longer fits; the enzyme is denatured
The enzyme is killed because it is a living organism
The enzyme turns into a carbohydrate
questions.answer: The shape of the active site changes so the substrate no longer fits; the enzyme is denatured
questions.hint: Enzymes are proteins; think about what heat does to their shape.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain how increasing the temperature from 20 °C to 37 °C affects the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction in the human body.
questions.hint: Use the ideas of kinetic energy, collisions and enzyme–substrate complexes.

bss.topic: Revisão do 1º term: da Proclamação da República à ditadura

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano foi proclamada a República no Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi no ano seguinte ao da abolição da escravidão.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual lema positivista foi colocado na bandeira republicana?
questions.hint: O positivismo valorizava a ordem social e o avanço científico.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como ficou conhecido o acordo em que as elites de São Paulo e Minas Gerais se alternavam na Presidência durante a Primeira República?
questions.hint: Pense nos principais produtos de cada estado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamava o voto controlado pelos coronéis, em que o eleitor votava no candidato indicado pelo chefe local?
questions.hint: O nome vem de um objeto usado para conduzir cavalos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Segundo a Constituição de 1891, como era o voto no Brasil?
options: Secreto e aberto a todos os adultos
Aberto e restrito a homens alfabetizados maiores de 21 anos
Secreto e obrigatório para homens e mulheres
questions.answer: Aberto e restrito a homens alfabetizados maiores de 21 anos
questions.hint: Lembre quem ficava de fora: mulheres e analfabetos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual revolta, ocorrida no Rio de Janeiro em 1904, foi uma reação à vacinação obrigatória e às reformas urbanas?
questions.hint: O nome da revolta lembra a campanha de saúde.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Contra o que lutaram os marinheiros na Revolta da Chibata, em 1910?
options: A cobrança de impostos sobre o café
questions.hint: A chibata era um chicote.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que movimento armado encerrou a Primeira República em 1930?
questions.hint: O nome traz o próprio ano.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano o Código Eleitoral garantiu o direito de voto às mulheres no Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi dois anos depois do fim da Primeira República.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas características marcou o Estado Novo, de 1937 a 1945?
options: Eleições diretas e liberdade de imprensa
Fechamento do Congresso, censura e governo centralizado
Divisão do poder entre os coronéis
questions.answer: Fechamento do Congresso, censura e governo centralizado
questions.hint: Pense em um regime autoritário.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que sigla designa o conjunto de leis trabalhistas reunido em 1943, que inclui carteira de trabalho e férias?
questions.hint: São três letras: Consolidação, Leis e Trabalho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual característica marcou o período democrático de 1946 a 1964?
options: Partido único e ausência de eleições
Eleições diretas para presidente e vários partidos
Governo exercido por uma junta de militares
questions.answer: Eleições diretas para presidente e vários partidos
questions.hint: A Constituição de 1946 restaurou direitos democráticos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual empresa estatal foi criada em 1953, após a campanha "O petróleo é nosso"?
questions.hint: O nome da empresa vem do recurso natural da campanha.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Uma fonte de 1968 diz: "Fica suspensa a garantia de habeas corpus nos casos de crimes políticos". A qual medida da ditadura esse trecho se refere?
questions.hint: Foi o mais duro dos atos institucionais.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Um cartaz de 1984 diz: "Eu quero votar para presidente". A que movimento ele está ligado?
questions.hint: Na época, o presidente era escolhido de forma indireta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que a censura à imprensa foi importante para a manutenção da ditadura militar (1964–1985).
questions.hint: Pense no que acontece quando a população não recebe informações sobre o governo.

bus.topic: Review: understanding business activity and motivation

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which sector of the economy includes farming, fishing and mining?
questions.hint: This sector extracts natural resources.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the sector of the economy that a hotel belongs to.
questions.hint: Hotels provide services.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What type of business is owned and controlled by one person who has unlimited liability?
questions.hint: Think of the simplest form of business ownership.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which feature applies to a private limited company?
options: Shares can be sold to the general public on the stock exchange
It is owned by the government
questions.hint: Think about what 'limited' in the name refers to.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an internal stakeholder?
questions.hint: Internal stakeholders work within the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which objective is most likely for a social enterprise?
options: Achieve social or environmental aims as well as make a profit
Increase the owner's personal wealth only
questions.answer: Achieve social or environmental aims as well as make a profit
questions.hint: The word 'social' is a clue.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which pair of stakeholder objectives is most likely to conflict?
options: Shareholders want higher dividends; employees want higher wages
Customers want quality; managers want quality
Government wants taxes paid; owners want to follow the law
Suppliers want to be paid; owners want good suppliers
questions.answer: Shareholders want higher dividends; employees want higher wages
questions.hint: Both groups want a share of the same profit.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business has revenue of $50,000 and total costs of $38,000. Calculate its profit in dollars.
questions.hint: Profit = revenue − total costs.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A café sells 400 sandwiches at $12.50 each. Calculate its revenue in dollars.
questions.hint: Revenue = price × quantity.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm's sales rose from $200,000 to $250,000. Calculate the percentage increase.
questions.hint: Divide the change by the original value, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In the hierarchy of needs, which level must be satisfied first?
questions.hint: Think about food, water and shelter.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A factory worker is paid $2 for every item produced. Which payment method is this?
questions.hint: Pay depends on the number of pieces made.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a non-financial method of motivation?
questions.hint: It does not involve giving the worker money.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In a franchise, what does the franchisee usually pay to the franchisor?
options: A fee and a royalty on sales
questions.answer: A fee and a royalty on sales
questions.hint: The franchisee pays to use the brand.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for a sole trader of changing into a private limited company.
questions.hint: Think about liability, raising finance and sharing control.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A bakery has high staff turnover. Analyse how job enrichment could improve the motivation of its employees.
questions.hint: Think about responsibility, interesting work and how staff might feel.

chem.topic: Review: particles, atomic structure, bonding and stoichiometry

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is an isotope?
options: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Atoms of different elements with the same mass
questions.answer: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
questions.hint: Isotopes have the same number of protons.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: An atom of chlorine has atomic number 17 and mass number 35. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.hint: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Write the electronic configuration of sodium (atomic number 11).
questions.hint: Fill the shells with 2, then 8, then the rest.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How is an ionic bond formed?
options: By transferring electrons from a metal to a non-metal
By a sea of delocalised electrons
questions.answer: By transferring electrons from a metal to a non-metal
questions.hint: Ions form when atoms gain or lose electrons.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is a covalent bond?
options: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
The attraction between oppositely charged ions
The attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons
questions.answer: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
questions.hint: Covalent bonds usually form between non-metal atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Write the formula of aluminium oxide.
questions.hint: Aluminium forms 3+ ions and oxide ions are 2−.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why does sodium chloride have a high melting point?
options: It has strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions in a giant lattice
It is made of small molecules
questions.answer: It has strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions in a giant lattice
questions.hint: Think about the type of structure in an ionic compound.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity?
options: Each carbon atom has one delocalised electron that can move
It has a giant ionic lattice
Its layers are held by strong covalent bonds
questions.answer: Each carbon atom has one delocalised electron that can move
questions.hint: Each carbon forms only three covalent bonds.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances such as water have low boiling points?
questions.hint: Boiling separates molecules, not atoms inside them.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Ammonia (Mr 17) and hydrogen chloride (Mr 36.5) are released at opposite ends of a tube. Which gas diffuses faster?
questions.hint: Compare the relative molecular masses.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of carbon dioxide, CO2. (Ar: C = 12, O = 16)
questions.hint: Add the mass of one carbon and two oxygens.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the number of moles in 9.0 g of water (Mr = 18).
questions.hint: Moles = mass ÷ Mr.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the mass, in grams, of 0.25 mol of calcium carbonate, CaCO3 (Mr = 100).
questions.hint: Mass = moles × Mr.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. Calculate the mass, in grams, of magnesium oxide formed from 6.0 g of magnesium. (Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16)
questions.hint: Find the moles of Mg first, then use the mole ratio.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm³, of a solution containing 0.2 mol of solute in 500 cm³ of solution.
questions.hint: Convert cm³ to dm³ first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why diamond is very hard.
questions.hint: Think about how many bonds each carbon atom forms and the type of structure.

comp.topic: Term 1 review: data representation, transmission and algorithm design

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the denary number 45 to an 8-bit binary number.
questions.hint: Start with the largest place value that fits into 45.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 3F to denary.
questions.hint: Each hex digit is worth 16 times the digit to its right.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An image is 800 × 600 pixels with a colour depth of 24 bits. Calculate its file size in bytes.
questions.hint: File size = width × height × colour depth, then divide by 8.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A mono sound file is sampled at 44 100 Hz with a sample resolution of 16 bits for 10 seconds. Calculate its file size in bytes.
questions.hint: Multiply sample rate × resolution × time, then divide by 8.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement describes serial data transmission?
options: Several bits are sent at the same time on several wires
Data is sent one bit at a time over a single wire
Data can only travel in one direction
questions.answer: Data is sent one bit at a time over a single wire
questions.hint: Think of cars in a single lane.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which transmission mode allows data to travel in both directions, but only one direction at a time?
questions.hint: A walkie-talkie works this way.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: The 7-bit data 1011001 is sent using even parity. What parity bit (0 or 1) must be added?
questions.hint: Count the 1s already in the data.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which error detection method uses acknowledgements and timeouts to request that data is re-sent?
questions.hint: The sender waits for a reply from the receiver.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is a feature of symmetric encryption?
options: The same key is used to encrypt and decrypt
The public key decrypts the data
questions.answer: The same key is used to encrypt and decrypt
questions.hint: 'Symmetric' means both sides are the same.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of compression permanently removes some data from a file?
questions.hint: The name suggests something is lost.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
total ← 0
FOR i ← 1 TO 4
  total ← total + i * 2
NEXT i
OUTPUT total
What value is output?
questions.hint: Trace the loop, writing down total after each pass.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which validation check makes sure that an exam mark is between 0 and 100?
questions.hint: The check looks at the lowest and highest allowed values.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How does a linear search find an item in a list?
options: It checks each item in turn from the start
It always checks the middle item first
It sorts the list before searching
It only checks the last item
questions.answer: It checks each item in turn from the start
questions.hint: 'Linear' means in a line.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain two reasons why programmers often use hexadecimal instead of binary.
questions.hint: Think about how long binary numbers are and how easy they are to read.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the 7-bit binary number 1011011 to denary.
questions.hint: Add the place values 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 where there is a 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the 7-bit binary number 1101011 to hexadecimal.
questions.hint: Add a leading 0 to make 8 bits, then split into two groups of 4.
